topic: The guard does not judge what a cwd contains in block-other-jobs
detail: SP-040 judges a cd_dest, path, git dir or glob prefix that contains another job's root as reaching that job, but the call's cwd only in strict mode. Otherwise every call of a session started under a public root such as ~/code (which holds every job's root) would be refused. So in block-other-jobs a command that searches its cwd by default (grep -r x, rg x, find, du, tar) run with cwd ~/code is allowed, and the OS sandbox (SP-046) is the boundary. Options: keep this; or refuse such calls when the command is a known recursive reader with no path argument (needs Targets to report it); or pin public-root sessions out of ancestor cwds.
